Because I own this same jean I watched this video with much interest. I noticed quite a few differences between your 1947 Levi’s 501 LVC and mine. The buttons on the fly on yours look shiny and silvery, whereas mine are copper. Also it appears yours have only 4 buttons including the waist button, whereas mine have 5. This is interesting because I have worn Levis 501s for decades, and have 10 pairs. My older 501s from the 70s have 5 buttons, (I’m not such a geek that I can specifically date any of them) but more recent modern 501s only have 4 buttons. Also yours were made in Turkey and mine were made in the USA. I bought mine from a friend who paid $260 but didn’t follow your rule, and they shrank up a lot so as to no longer fit him: his loss, my gain. I have to say that your claim that yours did not fit is IMO a perfect fit on you except for the winpy roll-up cuff - you need 2 inches longer to make this look right. If the waist is too tight, dip the waist in water mixed with a good dose of fabric softener, let soak for an hour, then use a waist stretcher (the solid build of the LVC handle take this no prob) and air dry for a couple of days to give yourself a good inch or more. When I was a teen, our method was in summer to put on our brand-new shrink to fit 501s and sit in a bathtub as hot and for as long as we could stand it in the morning, then go out and mess around all day long allowing the 501s to dry on us so as to shrink to the form of our bodies. Our moms were furious as the bath water was stained deep indigo which was not easy to Ajax off the bathtub.
